attributes.law_screen: claim.law.swap-loop-is-record-layout-ground-truth: APPLIED as the standard to meet, and the buffer FAILS it -- there is no swap loop or equivalent whole-record traversal over this buffer anywhere in the TU (ShopLoadData's swap loop covers DSItem, a different record), so no ground-truth field ordering exists. claim.law.walked-base-symbol-identity and claim.law.local-alias-vs-direct-global-spelling-diverges: APPLIED and decisive -- both warn that which symbol a base is spelled against is codegen-visible, which is exactly what the measurement then confirmed; they are the reason the respelling was gated rather than assumed safe. claim.law.offsetof-hazard-is-per-base-not-per-function: APPLIED, considered before touching a base shared by six functions. claim.law.sizeof-defeats-loop-stride-induction: screened, not applicable, no sizeof stride was introduced in shop.c. claim.law.lwzu-idiom-web-retention: screened, not applicable, none of the converted expressions is a load-update idiom. claim.law.multifield-alias-defeats-indexed-addressing and claim.law.declared-alias-vs-repeated-cast: screened, not reached, the pass never got as far as choosing an alias form because the base-identity question was refuted first.
attributes.residual: All ~56 sites LEFT RAW, deliberately, and this is the honest-miss outcome the work order asked for rather than a failure to try. Two independent blockers, each sufficient on its own. (1) Symbol separation is REFUTED, not merely unhelpful: the target reaches 336/4432/5456/6480 from one lbl_802897D0 relocation plus immediate adds, so the over-run that looks like the defect is actually what the original C compiled to -- see the new law. (2) Names are unavailable: the Xbox SHOP.OBJ roster's ~26 globals are all 4/16/48 bytes and none is large enough to be any of the five big GC tables (four 1KB, one 3KB), their order differs from GC's, and no PDB struct covers the region -- so the small arrays cannot be assigned one-to-one and the big ones have no counterpart at all. Adopting names would have been invention. What IS now settled and did not exist before this pass: the buffer is ONE object of at least 7680 bytes, and its full region map tiles exactly with no slack (see the map claim). A future structdraft is therefore a naming problem only, and the map claim names the two concrete ways to close it. DO NOT re-run the symbol-separation axis; it is measured, not guessed.
